more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
more_info.overview: Sodium nitrate is an inorganic sodium salt of the nitrate ion, used in specified preservative applications. Its preservative role is to limit spoilage caused by microorganisms and extend the storage life of the food. The specified material is supplied as white powder or crystalline material.
more_info.daily_intake: 0–3.7 mg nitrate ion/kg body weight/day (JECFA, 1995). The evaluation excludes infants below three months.
more_info.side_effects:
Exposure from additive uses was a small part of total dietary nitrate.
All-source exposure could exceed the limit; conversion to nitrite is relevant to the assessment.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain ripened cheese; whey cheese; non-heat–treated meat products; processed fish and fishery products including molluscs and crustaceans; dairy analogues, including beverage whiteners.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
